statements.label: Timing
statements.text: Spring when water warms; roughly April-June in the Southeast; later and shorter farther north; warm or heated water can see a long or second (August) spawn.

statements.label: Temperature
statements.text: 59-75 F; peak about 65 F; Science ranges 15-24 C (59-75 F); 18-22 C (64-72 F) optimum (FAO); bowfisher reports: moving shallow at ~60 F, spawning from ~62 F, peak 65-68 F, over by ~80 F…

statements.label: Habitat
statements.text: Shallow, warm, slow or still water with submerged or flooded vegetation; eggs are sticky and adhere to plants. Rising water that floods grass, fields and bank vegetation triggers and supports spawning.

statements.label: Shallow movement
statements.text: Adults move into water often less than 1 m (sometimes backs exposed) in coves, backwaters, flooded margins; males arrive first.

statements.label: Pre-spawn
statements.text: As water nears about 15-16 C (60 F) fish stage and move toward warming shallow bays, backwaters and tributary mouths; smaller males arrive first, larger females later.

statements.label: Post-spawn
statements.text: Fish disperse back to main lake/river habitat; may keep feeding in shallows into late summer. Falling water after a flood pulse draws fish off newly flooded margins.

statements.label: What triggers movement
statements.text: Warming toward 15-16 C (about 60 F) with longer days starts shallow movement; rising water plus warming is the strongest combined cue.

statements.label: Pre-spawn
statements.text: Staging and shallow movement from about 55-62 F.

statements.label: Spawn
statements.text: About 62-72 F with peak near 65-68 F by bowfisher accounts; science range 15-24 C.

statements.label: Summer
statements.text: Tolerates and uses 28-33 C; not pushed out of shallows by heat alone; oxygen below about 3 mg/L reduces feeding and growth.

statements.label: Cold-water slowdown
statements.text: Sluggish and aggregated below roughly 10 C; low shootable-shallow use in deep winter except at warm inflows/discharges.

statements.label: Shallow when
statements.text: Spring spawn run, over flooded vegetation, warm sunny afternoons in spring, and dusk-to-dawn in summer in small or shallow waters.

statements.label: Deeper when
statements.text: Winter cold; possibly summer nights in at least one run-of-river reservoir; after spawn when fish disperse.

statements.label: Useful depth and habitat
statements.text: Roughly 0-1.5 m in shallow coves and flats; spawning depth in southern accounts up to about 6 ft (1.8 m). In shallow southern lakes (mean depth about 1 m) carp are present lake-wide.

statements.label: Rising water
statements.text: Rising water that floods vegetated shore strongly pulls carp into the new shallows to spawn and feed; floodplain studies show most fish move onto flooded areas.

statements.label: Falling water
statements.text: Fish withdraw from flooded margins within days-weeks as water falls; many return to a prior home site.

statements.label: Flooded shoreline
statements.text: Prime: flooded grass, fields, brush are used for spawning and feeding.

statements.label: Current
statements.text: Prefer slack or slow water; tailraces hold early-season fish weeks before lake fish peak.

statements.label: River discharge
statements.text: Moderate rises help; strong flood current pushes fish to slack margins and backwaters.

statements.label: Backwater connection
statements.text: Connected backwaters and sloughs are major spawning and feeding sites; barriers can cut off spawning access.

statements.label: vegetationAssociation
statements.text: Spawning is tied to submerged/flooded vegetation (egg attachment). Adults occur without vegetation in turbid lakes, so vegetation matters for spawning more than for adult presence.

statements.label: coverAndSubstrate
statements.text: Soft mud/silt bottoms in shallow muddy coves with fallen branches, trees, reeds; also dike fields, sand disposal areas, rocky outcrops and steep or gentle banks. No stable substrate rule.

statements.label: Day
statements.text: Spawn and basking in shallows on warm spring days; wary in clear water.

statements.label: Dusk
statements.text: Activity rises, move to feeding shallows.

statements.label: Night
statements.text: Active, often shallower in lakes/ponds; one run-of-river reservoir study found them deeper and less active at night (conflict).

statements.label: Dawn
statements.text: Second activity peak around early morning.

statements.label: Bright sun
statements.text: Warm bright days in spring bring spawners into shallow muddy bays and make surface activity visible.

statements.label: Low light
statements.text: Activity peaks near midnight and early morning in pond telemetry; dusk-dawn feeding.

statements.label: Turbid water
statements.text: Carp thrive in very turbid water (Secchi 0.1-0.35 m); presence does not drop, but shootability does.

statements.label: Clear water
statements.text: Fish are spookier in clear water; large fish over about 10 lb are wary of boats.

statements.label: Main river
statements.text: Slack edges, eddies, backwater mouths, wing-dam/dike pockets; tailrace pools early spring.

statements.label: Reservoir
statements.text: Shallow muddy coves and flats, embayment heads.

statements.label: Creek / tributary
statements.text: Creek mouths and lower tributaries on rises; inflow confluences in winter.

statements.label: Backwater / slough
statements.text: Key spawn and feed habitat when connected.

statements.label: Shoreline / flat
statements.text: Flooded grass flats in spring; primary shooting habitat.

statements.label: Channel edge
statements.text: Staging/transit and deeper summer-day holding.

bowfisherGuide.takeaway: A bowfisher looking for common carp should concentrate on shallow, muddy, vegetated or newly flooded coves, backwaters and creek mouths when water reaches about 60-72 F in spring (especially on a rising or just-stable stage after rain), then on dusk-to-early-morning shallow flats through summer, and should treat cold winter water and strongly falling stages as low-odds.
